summary.prose: Every supported language records the calls its code makes, and a call that sits in no function is credited to its file. In TypeScript that is every test('…', () => { … }) body; Python and Go, which recorded no calls at all, now record them the way TypeScript does. The code review also recognises Python, Go and JVM test files, so tests in those languages reach the code they exercise.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Record calls made in module-level statements, so tests reach the code they call

api.name: walkNode
api.signature: walkNode(node: SyntaxNode, source: string, repo: string, repoId: number, filePath: string, lang: Language, fileId: string, now: string, entities: Entity[], relations: Relation[]): void

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.purpose: The file entity id, now also the caller of calls with no enclosing entity.

postconditions: A program-level statement that is not an import, function, class, interface, type alias or lexical/variable declaration (expression_statement, if/for/while/try/block/labeled) has extractCalls run over it with fileId as caller; the walk into its children continues as today.

For a lexical/variable declaration at program level or inside an export_statement, each declarator whose value is not an arrow_function, function_expression or generator_function_expression has extractCalls run over its value with fileId as caller; function-valued declarators keep today's entity and caller.

An export_statement with a `value` (export default <expr>) has extractCalls run over the value with fileId as caller; an exported function or class declaration is walked as today and is never scanned with the file as caller.
Calls inside function declarations, class bodies and function-valued declarators are not also credited to the file unless they are nested inside a statement the file is credited for.

api.name: walkPythonNode
api.signature: walkPythonNode(node: SyntaxNode, repo: string, repoId: number, filePath: string, fileId: string, now: string, entities: Entity[], relations: Relation[], allNames: Set<string> | null, hasAll: boolean, isTopLevel: boolean): void
postconditions: Each function/method entity's body emits CALLS {file, repo} per distinct callee name: an identifier callee as written, an attribute callee as its last attribute name; a small built-in set (print, len, range, isinstance, super, str, int, dict, list, set, tuple, ...) is skipped; nested defs and lambdas inside the body credit the enclosing entity.
A program-level statement that is not a function/class definition, decorated definition or import has its calls emitted with fileId as caller.
The existing HTTP and messaging walks are unchanged.

api.name: walkGoNode
api.signature: walkGoNode(node: SyntaxNode, repo: string, repoId: number, filePath: string, fileId: string, now: string, entities: Entity[], relations: Relation[]): void
postconditions: Each function and method entity's body emits CALLS {file, repo} per distinct callee name: an identifier as written, a selector expression as its field name; Go built-ins (make, len, cap, append, new, panic, recover, copy, delete, print, println, close) are skipped; function literals inside the body credit the enclosing entity.
Program-level var/const initializers have their calls emitted with fileId as caller.
The existing HTTP and messaging walks are unchanged.

api.name: isTestFile

returns.meaning: True for the existing TS/JS conventions and also test_*.py, *_test.py, *_test.go, any src/test/ directory, *Test.java/.kt/.scala and *Spec.scala.

postconditions: Every path the current predicate accepts is still accepted.

dataModelChanges.details: A CALLS (or CALLS_HTTP) relation may now have a file entity as its source (calls with no enclosing entity), and the Python and Go parsers now emit CALLS {meta:{file, repo}} with bare callee names, as the TS and JVM parsers do. No new entity kind, no new field, no store schema change.

errorCases.scenario: A file is re-indexed or deleted after its calls were recorded.
errorCases.detection: indexFile and fileEvent delete the file's entities (src/indexer/index.ts:1041, :785); the cascade removes incident edges and deleteUnresolvedForFile removes pending CALLS rows.
errorCases.response: Nothing new: CALLS from the file entity and from Python/Go entities follow the same clean-up.

errorCases.scenario: A Python or Go callee cannot be resolved by the cross-file pass (a library call, a dynamic call, a Go same-package call in another file).
errorCases.detection: resolveCall returns unresolved, ambiguous or no-candidate as for TS and JVM rows today.
errorCases.response: The row is kept as pending, classed by the existing rules (Epic c2ba6fa6 s1); it does not block completeness unless it awaits a target.
errorCases.userImpact: Those calls are not graph edges yet; Go same-package calls are the named open question.

migration.stateBefore: Per s1: the TS parser extracts calls only inside function declarations, class methods and function-valued declarators (src/indexer/parser/typescript.ts:259, :419, :552); the Python and Go parsers emit no CALLS (src/indexer/parser/python.ts:124-126, src/indexer/parser/go.ts:114-116); isTestFile recognises only TS/JS test files (src/workflow/code-review/grounding.ts:60-62).
migration.stateAfter: Calls with no enclosing entity are CALLS from the file entity (TS, Python, Go); Python and Go emit CALLS from functions and methods; isTestFile recognises Python, Go and JVM test files.

migrationSteps.action: Add the TS module-level and export handling to walkNode.
Add the general CALLS walk to the Python parser, with program-level calls credited to the file.
Add the general CALLS walk to the Go parser, with package-level initializer calls credited to the file.
Extend isTestFile with the Python, Go and JVM test conventions.
Update and restart the installed daemon, then reindex the registered repositories so every file gains its new CALLS.

migration.backwardCompat: No store schema change and no new entity kind. Until a file is re-parsed it keeps its old edges, so a full reindex is needed. Python and Go repositories gain many pending CALLS rows on the first reindex; they are classed by the existing rules.

alternativesConsidered.name: Calls with no enclosing entity go to the file entity; Python and Go get a general CALLS walk; isTestFile learns the other languages
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: TS module-level and exported-initializer calls become CALLS from the file entity; Python and Go emit CALLS like TS does; the review recognises Python, Go and JVM test files.
alternativesConsidered.approach: TypeScript: walkNode extracts calls with the file entity as caller for a program-level statement that is not a declaration it handles, for each non-function declarator value of a program-level or exported lexical/variable declaration, and for an export_statement's `value` (export default <expr>); export unwrapping passes the module-level context into the declaration and never scans an exported function or class wholesale. Python: a walk over each function/method body emits CALLS {file, repo} per distinct callee (bare name: identifier, or the attribute's last name), skipping a small built-in set, beside the existing HTTP walk; program-level statements that are not definitions or imports are walked with the file entity as caller. Go: the same walk over each function and method body (callee = identifier, or the selector's field name), and program-level var/const initializers with the file entity. isTestFile also matches test_*.py, *_test.py, *_test.go, a src/test/ directory, and *Test.java/.kt/.scala and *Spec.scala.
pros: No new entity kind and no store schema change.
Python and Go repos get a call graph at all; tests in every supported language can reach code.
cons: More CALLS rows (Python, Go) for the cross-file pass to resolve.
Go calls between files of one package stay unresolved until the resolver treats a package as one scope (open question).

alternativesConsidered.name: A synthetic entity per test call, plus Python/Go CALLS
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: As a1 for Python and Go, but each TS test('title', ...) becomes its own entity.
alternativesConsidered.approach: As a1, except the TS module-level calls inside a recognised test-runner call get a new entity per call named by its title.
cons: A new EntityKind with its graph-key byte mapping and a store schema step on the live v5 store.
The review joins callers to the test record per file, so the granularity is unused.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Adds a new EntityKind and a store schema step on the live v5 store for test-title granularity the code review does not use (it joins callers to the test record per file).

alternativesConsidered.name: TypeScript only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Fix module-level TS calls and leave Python and Go without CALLS.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The TS part of a1 only.
cons: Does not meet the ISSUE: Python and Go still record no calls.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates fixIntent-3: Python and Go still record no calls.

openQuestions: ts1 (partial): the standalone story carries no acceptance criteria; the test strategy maps three derived from the approved issue's fix intent (ac1 TS calls with no enclosing entity are CALLS from the file, ac2 Python and Go emit CALLS, ac3 the review recognises test files in every supported language and their callers reach the grounding) [c7].

Go calls between files of one package have no import to resolve through (src/indexer/cross-file-resolver.ts:474-510), so Go tests in the same package will not reach the code until the resolver treats a Go package as one scope. That resolver is being changed by Epic c2ba6fa6 Story s1; decide whether it joins this Story, s1, or a separate issue [c3].
Kotlin and Scala DSL-style tests written in a class body (test("x") { ... }) were not checked [c2].
